inferred_requirements.title: Password Reset Session Invalidation
inferred_requirements.description: Upon a successful password reset event, the system must invalidate all active refresh tokens associated with the user identity.
inferred_requirements.justification: Directly stated in the prompt requirements.

inferred_requirements.title: Cross-Cluster Token Blacklisting
inferred_requirements.description: Refresh token invalidation must propagate across all application clusters to ensure immediate revocation globally.
inferred_requirements.justification: Directly stated in the prompt requirements ('across all clusters').

inferred_requirements.title: Distributed Revocation Synchronization Mechanism
inferred_requirements.description: The system requires a distributed state synchronization mechanism (e.g., distributed cache or event bus) to instantly synchronize token revocation states across cluster boundaries.
inferred_requirements.justification: Why 1: Refresh tokens are verified locally across multiple clusters without central bottleneck. -> Why 2: A password reset in Cluster A must instantly prevent token reuse in Cluster B. -> Why 3: Mandatory Invariant: Revocation state must be globally consistent or use a distributed blacklist/revocation timestamp within bounded replication lag.

inferred_requirements.title: Token Storage and Revocation Verification Format
inferred_requirements.description: The exact storage engine, database schema, caching technology (e.g., Redis, PostgreSQL), and token format (e.g., JWT, opaque tokens) are not specified.
inferred_requirements.justification: The prompt does not state the underlying storage tier, caching provider, or token format standard.

inferred_requirements.title: Third-Party Authentication and Billing UI
inferred_requirements.description: User avatar upload interfaces, social login OAuth providers, and credit card billing management features are excluded.
inferred_requirements.justification: Explicitly restricted by domain guidance to prevent unrequested scope expansion.
